# navigation


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

`NavBar` renders a `<header navbar>` with a brand link, a `<nav>` region
for links and collapsible controls such as search, and an optional `end`
group for actions such as an account menu.

``` python
from fasthtml.common import H1, P
from answerui.registry import reg
from answerui.layout import Stack, Cluster
from answerui.surfaces import Badge
from answerui.demo import demo
```

## Navbar

By default, `NavBar` uses the page background (`--color-background`)
with a bottom hairline border (`--color-border`) and places the brand,
navigation, and end actions on one row. Links appear as plain text. Mark
the current link with `aria_current='page'` to highlight it with the
accent wash (`--v-3` background and `--v2` text, or `--tint` on a
`vivid` bar).

Pass `align='center'` to centre `<nav>` between the brand and end
actions, or `align='end'` to align `<nav>` beside `end` (the default
`align='start'` places links right after the brand). Pass `sticky=True`
to keep the bar pinned to the top while scrolling. Pass `vivid=True` for
an accent surface (`--color-accent` with `--color-on-accent` text), and
`theme='light'` or `theme='dark'` to override the inherited colour
scheme (`ui-theme`).

When `collapse=True` and navigation items are passed, `NavBar` adds a
disclosure button. The shared `mountNavbar` controller measures the
actual row width instead of using a fixed viewport breakpoint, and hides
`<nav>` behind that button whenever the row overflows. Opening the
disclosure shows the same `<nav>` in normal flow below the bar without
duplicating its content. Clicking a link, clicking outside the bar, or
pressing Escape closes the menu. Pressing Escape returns focus to the
disclosure button. Content passed as `end` stays visible in the bar.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### NavBar

``` python
def NavBar(
    brand, *c, end:tuple=(), href:str='/', label:str='Main navigation', align:str='start', sticky:bool=False,
    vivid:bool=False, theme:NoneType=None, collapse:bool=False, **attrs
):
```

*A brand, navigation links and actions sharing a responsive row*

In this dashboard example, the links and search field go into the
collapsible `<nav>` while the account menu stays visible in `end`. The
menu trigger wraps an `Avatar` with `aria_label='Account'`. Shared CSS
styles an avatar button as a circle:

``` python
NavBar.demo(height='14rem')
```

``` html

  <div navbar-row>
<a href="/" navbar-brand>Acme</a><button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" btn-icon navbar-toggle aria-controls="_34RB-_K-RNuL3zo3R1oMLQ" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Navigation"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" aria-hidden="true" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-menu"></use></svg></button>    <nav aria-label="Main navigation" id="_34RB-_K-RNuL3zo3R1oMLQ">
<a href="#" aria-current="page">Overview</a><a href="#">Inventory</a><a href="#">Customers</a><a href="#">Products</a>      <div role="search">
        <input input type="search" placeholder="Search..." aria-label="Search">
      </div>
    </nav>
    <div navbar-end>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" aria-label="Account" popovertarget="_ywAYTlCzR7KkEDJChzDL2A"><span role="img" aria-label="Ada Lovelace" avatar style="--avatar-size: 1.75rem">AL</span></button>      <div popover="auto" popup dropdown id="_ywAYTlCzR7KkEDJChzDL2A">
<a href="#" menu-item>Profile</a><a href="#" menu-item>Settings</a><hr><button type="button" btn btn-variant="primary" menu-item popovertarget="_ywAYTlCzR7KkEDJChzDL2A" popovertargetaction="hide">Sign out</button>      </div>
    </div>
```

## Configurations

These options can be combined. The examples below show `align='center'`,
`align='end'` beside sign-in buttons in `end`, `vivid=True` with an
accent background, and `theme='dark'` on a light page:

``` python
def _auth(): return [Btn('Log in', variant='secondary'), Btn('Sign up')]
demo(Stack(
    NavBar('Acme', *_links(), align='center'),
    NavBar('Acme', *_links(), end=_auth(), align='end'),
    NavBar('Acme', *_links(), end=_auth(), vivid=True),
    NavBar('Acme', *_links(), end=_auth(), theme='dark')))
```

## Collapse

At `24rem` wide, the bar collapses because the links and search field do
not fit beside the brand. Open the disclosure menu to tab through the
links. The account menu stays visible in `end`.

``` python
demo(_navbar_example(), width='24rem', height='18rem')
```

## Customisation

You can register custom variants with `NavBar.variant` without editing
the shared stylesheet. Below, `reg.rule` defines `--column` (`42rem`).
Passing `glass=True` applies a translucent blurred background capped to
`--column`. `mountNavbar` still measures the row and collapses `<nav>`
on overflow. Scroll the preview to see content pass behind the bar:

``` python
reg.rule(':root { --column: 42rem; }', name='column', doc='The width of the content column.')

NavBar.variant('glass', r"""
background: oklch(from var(--n-2) l c h / .5); backdrop-filter: blur(16px) saturate(1.5);
max-inline-size: var(--column); margin: var(--space) auto 0; border: 1px solid var(--n-1); border-radius: var(--radius);
box-shadow: var(--floating);

""", doc='A translucent bar at the width of the content column.')

demo(Div(
    NavBar('Acme', A('About', href='#', aria_current='page'), A('Blog', href='#'), A('Contact', href='#'),
        end=Btn('Subscribe', variant='secondary'), sticky=True, glass=True, collapse=True),
    Stack(H1('Field notes'), Cluster(Badge('Design'), Badge('CSS', ui_tone='success'), Badge('FastHTML', ui_tone='warning'), cls='gap-2'),
        P('A short account of building a component library on the web platform, written as it happened.'),
        P('The first decision was to style native tags rather than invent new ones. Every form control the browser already has is already accessible, already keyboard-driven, and already known to assistive technology.'),
        P('The second was that colour should come from one hue. A single number sets the whole palette, and severity is a context rather than a variant.'),
        cls='mx-auto py-6 px-4', style='max-inline-size: var(--column)')),
    height='14rem')
```

``` html
<div>
  <header navbar navbar-align="start" navbar-sticky navbar-collapse glass>
    <div navbar-row>
<a href="/" navbar-brand>Acme</a><button type="button" btn btn-variant="quiet" btn-icon navbar-toggle aria-controls="_CryLK5VTSJepza6G7ssWow" aria-expanded="false" aria-label="Navigation"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewbox="0 0 24 24" height="24px" width="24px" aria-hidden="true" class="lucide-icon "><use href="#lc-menu"></use></svg></button>      <nav aria-label="Main navigation" id="_CryLK5VTSJepza6G7ssWow">
<a href="#" aria-current="page">About</a><a href="#">Blog</a><a href="#">Contact</a>      </nav>
      <div navbar-end>
<button type="button" btn btn-variant="secondary">Subscribe</button>      </div>
    </div>
  </header>
  <div stack class="mx-auto py-6 px-4" style="max-inline-size: var(--column)">
    <h1>Field notes</h1>
    <div cluster class="gap-2">
<span badge>Design</span><span badge ui-tone="success">CSS</span><span badge ui-tone="warning">FastHTML</span>    </div>
    <p>A short account of building a component library on the web platform, written as it happened.</p>
    <p>The first decision was to style native tags rather than invent new ones. Every form control the browser already has is already accessible, already keyboard-driven, and already known to assistive technology.</p>
    <p>The second was that colour should come from one hue. A single number sets the whole palette, and severity is a context rather than a variant.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```
